evidence.text: A person 各 welcomed under one's roof 宀; 各 also provides the pronunciation
Phonosemantic compound. 宀 represents the meaning and 各 represents the sound.
寄也。从宀各聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *kʰraːɡ): semantic 宀 (“roof”) + phonetic 各 (OC *klaːɡ) – a guest.
Probably belongs to the word family of 格 (OC *klaːɡ, *kraːɡ, “to go, to come”). Schuessler (2007) cites Tibetan དགྲ (dgra, “enemy”) as a possible cognate.
寄也。从宀各聲。

evidence.source: 小學堂文字學資料庫（中央研究院）
evidence.field: 客字形演變與構形說明
evidence.text: The entry catalogs 客 under Western Zhou bronze inscriptions (including 集成04214), Chu manuscripts, and Small Seal/說文. Its account says 宀 represents a house, while 各 has a ‘coming’ sense and also serves as the phonetic; the whole graph refers to someone arriving from outside. This supports a phonosemantic analysis, though the page does not reproduce a dated inscription text or establish that 各’s ‘coming’ sense was graphically intended in 客.
evidence.title: 漢字「客」：字形演變

evidence.source: 說文解字, quoted in Kotobank’s 字通 entry
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文, 卷七下:「寄也。从宀各聲」—‘to lodge/reside’; formed from 宀 with 各 as phonetic. This is an important historical lexicographic analysis, not direct confirmation of the graph’s original pictorial motivation.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary quotation in modern reference
evidence.title: 客（きゃく）とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.source: Kotobank, 精選版 日本国語大辞典 entry
evidence.text: The Japanese dictionary records 客 ‘visitor/invitee’ in 虎明本狂言・連歌盗人 (late Muromachi–early modern); the commercial-customer sense in 色道大鏡 (1678); and the travel/sojourner sense with citations including 和玉篇 (15th c.) and 曹植’s 門有万里客詩. These are Japanese lexicographic first-example records, not dates for the Chinese graph or necessarily the earliest Chinese word attestations.
evidence.title: 客（きゃく）とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.text: 字通 classifies 宀＋各 as 会意 and proposes that 各 depicts a spirit descending toward a ritual vessel, so 客 originally referred to a guest deity received inside a house; it cites 詩經 周頌「我客戾止」and「客戾止」 contexts as references to ancestral/guest spirits. This conflicts with the phonetic analysis and is presented as an interpretation, not demonstrated paleographic consensus.
evidence.title: 客（きゃく）とは？ 意味や使い方

evidence.field: Baxter–Sagart and Zhengzhang reconstructions; Middle Chinese fanqie
evidence.text: The entry gives Middle Chinese khaek, fanqie 苦格切, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *kʰˤrak (system 1.1/2014), and Zhengzhang *kʰraːɡ. The distinct systems should not be merged. Local Baxter–Sagart rows independently checked: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, row 1887: 客 kè/khaek, *kʰˤrak; row 1035: 各 gè/kak, *kˤak. These readings are compatible with 各 functioning as a phonetic component, while their differences prevent treating them as identical pronunciations.
evidence.kind: historical phonology reference cross-checked against local dataset
evidence.title: 客 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: 形義通解; 金文用例与语义延伸
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 客 as a Western Zhou bronze graph with 宀 for a house and 各 serving as phonetic while also suggesting arrival. It reports bronze uses for guests, a bronze example where 客 is borrowed for 各 ‘arrive’, and later extensions to travellers, envoys, specialists, customers, and a serving/portion classifier. It cites Mawangdui Laozi B, line 250, where manuscript 格 corresponds to transmitted 客. These are the database’s reported examples and analysis; they do not by themselves date every semantic extension.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 中央研究院, 漢字「客」：字形演變
evidence.text: The page catalogs a bronze form under 集成04214 and says 宀 represents a house, 各 has an ‘arrive’ sense and is also the phonetic, and the whole graph refers to someone coming from outside. It does not provide the dated inscription’s text on this page. This supports a phonosemantic analysis, while the semantic contribution attributed to 各 remains the database’s analysis.
evidence.title: 漢字「客」：字形演變

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No inspected original Western Zhou bronze inscription text or dated inscription context was obtained; the Sinica database identifies a Western Zhou bronze record and a catalog number but the graph images were not visually inspected.

No direct paleographic evidence establishes whether 客’s earliest semantic motivation was an ordinary visitor, a ritual guest spirit, or whether a later interpretation has conflated word sense and graph origin. The 会意/guest-deity account and phonosemantic account remain competing source assertions.

No systematic Chinese semantic chronology was established from a dictionary gloss sequence. The earliest graph attribution (Western Zhou bronze) and lexicographic sense in 說文 (‘to lodge/reside’) are documented separately; precise first contextual attestations for ordinary guest, traveller, resident, and customer senses remain unverified here.

The local HSK1 extract and full Unihan readings file did not cover either character. Official Unicode character-record URLs were attempted and failed in this web tool; external indexed readings were not substituted as verified official records.
No evidence was found here for the proposed word-family relation to 格 or the Tibetan comparison; neither is needed to establish 各’s phonetic role in 客.

A conflicting secondary interpretation in the dossier treats 客 as a 会意 graph referring to a guest deity; fresh inspected pages support the phonosemantic analysis, but this pass did not retrieve and inspect the exact source page for that alternative. It therefore remains an unresolved competing account rather than a settled conclusion.

No dated original inscription text was inspected for the Sinica catalog item 集成04214, and the Commons vector was not visually inspected. Its stated source/object metadata is reported as page description only.

The database reports early bronze guest use and loan-like uses separately, but this pass did not establish a systematic, independently dated chronology for all later senses. Customer, traveller, specialist, and classifier extensions should not be ordered solely from gloss lists.

The proposed word-family relation to 格 and the Tibetan comparison were not independently established. 各’s phonetic role is supported by the traditional 說文 analysis and modern paleographic databases; no ancient object-name borrowing claim is made.

Exact local Baxter–Sagart TSV rows were not re-inspected in this invocation. The dossier reports 客 *kʰˤrak and 各 *kˤak in Baxter–Sagart notation; Oxford page inspection verified the work and reconstruction system context, not the individual character entries.
No exact current kMandarin values for both characters were verified from official Unihan records during this pass. Earlier dossier records report failed official lookups and missing local rows.

Commons file page open returned a cache-miss failure, and the direct upload URL attempt was inaccessible. Image identity and rights are based on the search-result description page, not pixel inspection.
Xiaoxuetang’s character query for 客 was unavailable with HTTP 401, so no query-returned image candidate could be assessed or selected.

The Commons file page describes a modern vector redraw of a mid-Western Zhou bronze-script form and states CC0, but the page could not be opened and the prior direct image URL returned 404. No alternate working direct image URL was verified; no glyph image is proposed.

The inspected paleographic entry catalogs a Western Zhou bronze form but does not provide its inscription text or a date for the cited object on the page. The source’s claim about 各’s semantic contribution is an analysis, not direct proof of original graphic motivation.
The sources give examples of older uses and later semantic developments, but this pass did not establish a systematic chronology for all senses or independently date every cited example.

The supplied dossier records a competing guest-deity analysis. This pass did not inspect that source directly, so the disagreement remains unresolved; the inspected sources support a phonosemantic analysis without establishing consensus.
This pass did not inspect exact local Baxter–Sagart TSV rows or successfully verify current kMandarin values for both 客 and 各; it makes no fresh claim about those readings.

limitations.text: No glyph image can be selected: the Commons candidate’s upload URL was unavailable, and the Academia Sinica character query did not return an image that could be assessed.
